title.narrative: Pacific Regional Initiative and Support for More Effective Counter-Trafficking in Persons (Pacific RISE CTIP)

description.narrative: (Pacific Islands Regional): .The Pacific Island region is reported as a source, transit point, and destination for human trafficking for purposes of sexual exploitation and forced labor particularly in local extractive industries such as fishing, logging, and mining. The annual U.S. State Department Trafficking in Persons report examines government actions to counter trafficking in persons relative to the minimum standards set in the Trafficking Victim Protection Act. The 2022 report's major finding is that a number of governments of Pacific Island Countries (PICs) do not fully meet the minimum standards for the elimination of trafficking. Papua New Guinea, Palau, and Tonga are on the Tier 2 watch list; and Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, Republic of Marshall Islands and Vanuatu are classified as Tier 2...This activity aims to combat trafficking in persons in the PICs through interventions that will reduce vulnerability to trafficking, enhance local and community-based mechanisms and strategies to prevent trafficking, provide adequate protection services and sustainable solutions to victims and survivors, and strengthen the capacity of relevant actors to expand access to legal services and remedies for victims and survivors, and prosecute traffickers. This activity will apply a holistic and multi-sectoral approach taking into consideration the priorities across the four pillars of the USG counter-trafficking strategy (prevention, protection, prosecution, and partnerships), the USAID Trafficking in Persons Policy, and the recommendations for the PICs as stated in the U.S. Department of State Annual Trafficking in Persons Reports..
